title: Diagrid on a freeform surface
summary: Divides any surface into a grid of bays and draws the two diagonals of every bay along the surface, producing a diagrid structure or facade pattern that follows the curvature.
how_to_use: Right-click 'Srf' and Set one Surface to use your own facade or roof surface (a sample is stored).
'Bays U' and 'Bays V' set how many diamonds you get in each direction.
Leave the four corner MD Sliders as they are for a classic diagrid; moving them bends the diagonals inside each bay.
Bake the two Curve On Surface components to get the diagonals.
concepts: Divide Domain2 + Isotrim: splitting a surface into sub-surfaces
Deconstruct Brep: faces, edges and vertices of a bay
Curve On Surface: a curve defined by UV points that stays on the surface

steps.title: 1  INPUTS - change these
steps.explain: The surface to cover and the number of bays in U and V.

steps.title: 2  Split the surface into bays
steps.explain: Divide Domain2 splits the surface's UV domain into Bays U x Bays V cells, and Isotrim cuts out one sub-surface per cell. Deconstruct Brep passes each bay on as a face.

steps.title: 3  Diagonal pattern (UV corners)
steps.explain: Each MD Slider is a point in the bay's own 0..1 UV space. (0,0)->(1,1) and (1,0)->(0,1) give the two diagonals; other values give other patterns.

steps.title: 4  RESULT - diagonals on every bay
steps.explain: Curve On Surface draws a curve through the UV points on every bay face, so the diagonals follow the surface exactly. Bake these to keep the diagrid.
